results.sentence: AI search agents that train each other without human answers drift into agreeing on the same wrong answers while their internal reward keeps rising, according to a preprint posted to arXiv on Sept. 30.
results.evidence: Opened the source; text and numbers match.

results.sentence: The 15-author paper, with researchers from Rutgers, UC San Diego, the University of Michigan, McGill and KFUPM, is not yet peer-reviewed.
results.evidence: arXiv abs: 'Meijia Chen and 14 other authors' = 15, confirmed. Affiliations are on the HTML full text only (cite 13, not 12): Rutgers (1 author), UCSD (2), Michigan (1), McGill (1), King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals (1), and 'Independent Researcher' (10 of 15). Corresponding authors: Tianyu Shi (McGill), Alaa Khamis (KFUPM). The listed institutions are accurate but the sentence omits that most authors are independent. 'KFUPM' is not used in the paper. 'Not yet peer-reviewed': arXiv v1 only; editorial preprint label is appropriate.
results.fix: The 15-author paper lists affiliations at Rutgers, UC San Diego, the University of Michigan, McGill and King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals; 10 of the 15 authors list themselves as independent researchers [13]. It is a preprint and has not been peer-reviewed.

results.sentence: Setup description (proposer, solver, reward at the frontier, no ground-truth check).
results.evidence: Uncited. Paper (full text, cites 13): 'a proposer turns source documents into questions and pseudo-labels, admitted pairs train a solver, and the solver's performance on new proposals determines the proposer reward ... shifts proposals toward the solver's current capability frontier, producing an automated curriculum without a fixed human-authored training set.' 'All treatments use the same backbone' (Qwen3.5-4B / 9B). Unsupported in the draft: 'two copies of one model teach each other', 'using web search' (paper says search agents with a tool budget), 'nobody checks answers against the truth' (the pseudo-labels are checked only by the post-hoc audit, which never feeds training).
results.fix: Add [[13]]. Suggested wording: 'In a self-evolving setup, a proposer turns source documents into questions with pseudo-labels, and a solver, built on the same Qwen3.5 backbone, is trained on them using search tools. The proposer is rewarded when the solver's answers agree with its pseudo-label on new questions, which pushes it toward the edge of the solver's ability. No human-written labels are used, so agreement stands in for being right [13].'

results.sentence: The authors call the failure co-cheating: "the proposer and solver increasingly agree on shared errors, so internal reward improves without a matching gain in external correctness".
results.evidence: Opened the source; text and numbers match.

results.sentence: They stress that it "does not imply intentional coordination".
results.evidence: Opened the source; text and numbers match.

results.sentence: In the standard Dr. Zero training loop, false agreement rose from 0.4% in round one to 6.1% by round three on Qwen3.5-4B, and from 0.3% to 8.8% on Qwen3.5-9B.
results.evidence: Opened the source; text and numbers match.

results.sentence: It helped only a little, cutting false agreement from 6.1% to 5.7% and from 8.8% to 7.2%.

results.sentence: The co-cheating agents drifted because their grader had trained on the same documents it scored.
results.evidence: Paper: auxiliary solver trained 'only on B' scores questions from A; 'excluding the evaluated source from the feedback solver prevents same-source errors from being systematically returned to the proposer' (cite 13). results.fix: The co-cheating agents drifted when the solver giving feedback had been trained on pseudo-labels from the same source documents it was scoring [13].
